title: Research
intro: Wang Lab connects skeletal muscle stem cell biology and regeneration with the ways aging changes repair. The work spans cellular and molecular regulation, genomics, computational approaches, and intervention studies.

themes.title: Muscle stem cells and the work of repair
themes.question: How do muscle stem cells remain ready to repair muscle and respond after injury?
paragraphs: Adult muscle stem cells (MuSCs) support muscle growth and repair. After injury, they activate, proliferate and differentiate; a portion of the population returns to a quiescent state.

The lab’s public studies examine intrinsic regulators of these state changes alongside signals from the surrounding niche. The Lockd–DHX36 study links a muscle-stem-cell regulator to myoblast proliferation and muscle regeneration.
approaches: Functional studies of muscle-stem-cell proliferation and regeneration

themes.title: Regeneration across an aging muscle
themes.question: How does age change skeletal muscle and the systems that support repair?
paragraphs: The lab’s public research record includes studies of age-associated changes in skeletal muscle, muscle stem cells and sarcopenia.

A 2025 study profiles young and aged human skeletal muscle using single-nucleus multi-omics and examines cellular senescence. A separate 2023 study maps three-dimensional genome organization across muscle-stem-cell lineage progression and aging.

themes.title: Changes within the cell and its surroundings
themes.question: How do cellular senescence and niche signaling appear in published studies of muscle aging and disease?
paragraphs: Two distinct lines in the public record address these questions. A 2025 study examines YY1–CCL5 signaling between muscle stem cells and niche cells in a Duchenne muscular dystrophy mouse model.
A separate 2026 publication focuses on cellular senescence in skeletal muscle regeneration. These papers are presented as related areas of inquiry, not as evidence for one shared mechanism.
approaches: Published study of niche signaling in a mouse model

themes.title: Regulation across RNA and genome organization
themes.question: How are RNA and chromatin regulators related to muscle stem-cell state and lineage progression?
paragraphs: Published studies in the lab’s record examine RNA processing, chromatin and genome organization in skeletal muscle stem cells. One study describes YTHDC1 as a regulator of mRNA splicing and nuclear export during muscle stem-cell activation and proliferation.

Other studies report three-dimensional genome reorganization during lineage progression and aging, and DNA G-quadruplex profiling in muscle stem cells. These works address different regulatory layers and remain individually linked to their publications below.

themes.title: From integrated profiles to intervention questions
themes.question: How can computational approaches and published profiles support the study of muscle aging and intervention?
paragraphs: The public publication list includes integrated profiling of aging human muscle and a 2026 computational tool for predicting chromatin-associated RNA-binding proteins. These are examples of computation and multi-omics in the record; biology remains the central question.

Published studies also examine intervention hypotheses in defined muscle-aging and muscular-dystrophy contexts. The sarcopenia paper describes Maraviroc as a senotherapeutic approach, while the dystrophic-muscle study discusses therapeutic intervention through the YY1–CCL5 axis. This page makes no claim of clinical efficacy.
approaches: Experimental study in defined disease contexts
